title: In vitro protein digestibility testing for novel foods and food improvement agents
summary: How simulated gastric digestion and SDS-PAGE analysis support novel protein safety assessment and regulatory submissions
body_markdown:
##
Analytical readout: SDS-PAGE


Samples are analyzed by sodium dodecyl sulfate polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE), a well-established separation technique that resolves proteins by molecular weight. This allows the study team to visualize the degradation profile of the test article over time and compare the banding pattern directly against the reference proteins. The result is a clear, interpretable dataset that documents whether the novel protein is digested in a manner consistent with conventional dietary proteins.


## What you need to provide


To initiate the study when working with Labcorp, you will need to supply the test article, which should be a characterized preparation of the protein of interest. Our team will work with you during the protocol phase to confirm the format, concentration, and quantity required prior to study start.


## Timelines


From study award and receipt of the test article, experimental work typically begins within the protocol completion phase and the full experimental phase runs approximately two weeks. A draft report is issued approximately four weeks following study completion. The total elapsed time from study award to draft report is typically eight to 10 weeks.


## A note on study scope


Because Labcorp operates a bespoke model rather than an off-the-shelf service approach, a novel food study design can be adapted to include additional phases, alternative incubation conditions, or modified readouts where your regulatory strategy requires it. That flexibility is intentional and will be addressed in the next blog post of this series.


## Part 3. When should you commission an *in vitro* digestibility study for your novel food or food improvement agent in development?


Protein digestibility data is typically submitted to regulatory authorities such as EFSA as part of a broader package that includes genotoxicity, chronic toxicology, ADME, and DART studies. Therefore, the study should be commissioned during pre-submission development, well before filing.


Because our *in vitro* digestibility studies are relatively fast to execute and do not require in vivo animal models, they can often be initiated earlier in the development timeline than other study types. This is an advantage worth planning around. Getting the digestibility data in hand early allows you to make informed decisions about how to frame the protein safety narrative in your dossier before the more complex, longer-lead studies are complete.


## What if the regulatory guidance is not clear yet?


At Labcorp, we design studies with complexity in mind. Where the regulatory requirement is to meet EFSA’s specific guidance for novel food protein characterization, we scope the study accordingly. Where additional data may be needed, we can discuss an expanded study design that addresses assessment needs within a single experimental program.


## What to expect from the data package


The report documents the study design, methodology, raw data, and a scientific evaluation of the digestibility of your test article relative to the reference proteins. This report is formatted for direct integration into your regulatory dossier.


## The importance of working with a lab that understands your program


Novel food and food improvement agent development is not a linear process. Ingredients evolve, regulatory guidance shifts, and development timelines compress. The value of working with Labcorp goes beyond any single study. Our team is structured to engage with your program as a scientific partner, not simply as a service provider. That means responsive communication, the ability to adapt study protocols when your needs change, and a team with the in-depth experience to help you interpret your data in the context of your broader regulatory strategy.
